sections.overview: The necklace carpetshark is a small, bottom-dwelling shark of southern Australia and part of the collar-carpetshark family.
sections.identification: It has a long, slender body with a broad black collar dotted white behind the head, plus pale spots and mottled brown fins. It reaches about 92 cm, though specimens are often smaller.
sections.habitat: It occurs around southern Australia, from eastern Victoria and Tasmania westward to southwestern Western Australia, in temperate coastal waters and on reefs, in bays and estuaries.
sections.diet: Museum Victoria reports that it feeds mainly on shellfish.
sections.behavior: It is mainly nocturnal, sheltering by day in caves, crevices, beneath ledges or among kelp; it forages after dark.
sections.reproduction: It is oviparous, but the details of its breeding biology are poorly known.
sections.ecology: Its close genus-mate P. sparsimaculatum is known from far fewer records and deeper water off Western Australia; P. variolatum has a much broader southern coastal range and is often found in shallower habitats.
sections.conservation: The most recent Australian fisheries assessment classifies it as Least Concern and Sustainable; this assessment does not mean that every local population has been monitored.
